item.title: Matthew Hayden drops 'more smoke' remark on Sandpapergate, questions Australia's handling of 2018 ball-tampering scandal
item.description: Eight years after the infamous Sandpapergate scandal rocked Australian cricket, the controversy surrounding the 2018 ball-tampering incident refuses to die down. Fresh revelations from Cameron Bancroft and Usman Khawaja have once again brought questions of accountability and transparency into focus, with former Australia opener Matthew Hayden now calling for a fair and independent assessment of the entire episode. Hayden believes several questions surrounding the Cape Town Test against South Africa remain unanswered and has urged Cricket Australia to establish a transparent process that allows everyone involved to present their version of events. "It's just undeniable that there is a lot more smoke to come out of this fire," Hayden said while speaking on JioStar's 'Sandpapergate: The Unsettled Debate'. The former opener stressed that Australian cricket needs to move beyond the original sanctions and establish whether the full extent of the incident was ever investigated. He also insisted that reconciliation and trust would remain difficult as long as doubts continued to surround the scandal. Hayden calls for independent inquiry, wants former players to have their say Hayden argued that Cricket Australia should take ownership of the process and consider an independent assessment to establish whether further investigation is warranted. "Whether it's with Cricket Australia or an independent assessment process, I think we need to ask specific questions, and we need to identify if there are grounds for further inquiry, and then proceed with a clear scope and a fair process for everyone involved. There has to be some ownership over the process. Reconciliation is never going to be there for as long as there are question marks over integrity and trust," he said. The 54-year-old also emphasised that the process should not be restricted to current players, adding that those who were part of the 2018 South Africa tour and have since retired should also be given an opportunity to speak in an official capacity. He specifically mentioned David Warner and Usman Khawaja, along with other former players who have recently spoken about the controversy. "It's unimaginable to think that the game can't actually get itself into a position where it at least understands a little bit further around the seriousness of this matter, and then come up with some sort of process that entitles not only the current players, but also the players that were involved in that series, who have now subsequently retired, David Warner and Usman Khawaja, to have their say in an official capacity, and the other three that have come out in support of it as well. I think as long as that gate remains open, there will be a distrust issue," Hayden added. What are the fresh Sandpapergate allegations? item.title: Marc Marquez overtakes Valentino Rossi - now only Angel Nieto and Giacomo Agostini have more titles
item.description: Motorsport photo Marc Marquez continues to cement his legacy in motorcycle racing and sport as a whole. If his return to the top in 2025, with an impeccable season until he was injured, already left everyone stunned, the legendary Cervera rider has pushed his limits once again in 2026, overcoming every obstacle thrown his way to claim his 10th world title, and his eighth in MotoGP. This is a tally that allows the Spaniard to continue breaking historical records. While many already consider him the greatest of all time, the #93 continues to strengthen his case with the numbers to back it up. And with the crown he secured this weekend at the Portuguese Grand Prix, he has reached milestones that many considered impossible in the modern era. One of those is the number of motorcycle racing world titles across all categories. Marquez has reached the landmark of 10 championships, moving ahead of several legends of the sport. With his 10 titles, Marquez has finally overtaken Valentino Rossi, who finished his career with nine, with his best opportunity to surpass that tally coming in 2015, when he ultimately lost out to Jorge Lorenzo amid the controversy surrounding Marc. Not only has Marquez surpassed the Doctor's tally, but also that of Mike 'The Bike' Hailwood, who won nine titles in the 1960s, and Italian Carlo Ubbiali, who achieved the same feat in the 1950s. As a result, Marquez now has only two legendary figures ahead of him: Angel Nieto and Giacomo Agostini. Nieto's '12+1' world titles appeared untouchable until just a few years ago, but the reality is that Marquez is now just three championships short of the man regarded as the father of Spanish motorcycle racing. item.title: Tom Jackson, ESPN’s longtime ‘NFL Primetime’ co-host, dead at 75
item.description: For nearly two decades of autumn Sunday nights, long before every touchdown was a tap away on your phone, the surest way to make sense of the NFL’s sprawling afternoon slate was to wait for Tom Jackson to break it down beside Chris Berman on NFL Primetime . Jackson, who spent 14 seasons anchoring the Denver Broncos’ famed “Orange Crush” defense before becoming one of ESPN’s most trusted football voices, has died at 75, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. His family informed the network of his death, and Schefter did not report a cause. Tom Jackson, a foundational player on the Denver Broncos’ “Orange Crush” defense and a fixture at ESPN as a Hall of Fame broadcaster in his post-NFL career, has died. He was 75. Jackson’s family informed ESPN of his death. A fourth-round pick by the Broncos in the 1973 draft out of Louisville, Jackson played in 191 regular-season games, including 177 starts. He also played in 10 playoff games over 14 seasons with the Broncos. For many football fans, however, Jackson’s second career act was how they knew him. He had a 29-year run at ESPN and was a mainstay alongside Chris Berman. — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 22, 2026 A fourth-round pick out of Louisville in 1973, Jackson spent his entire playing career in Denver, starting 177 of his 191 regular-season games and appearing in 10 more in the playoffs. As accomplished as he was on the field, most fans knew him through the 29 years he spent in ESPN’s studio, most of them seated beside Berman. That partnership began in 1987, when Jackson went straight from the Broncos to Bristol as ESPN assembled its first serious slate of NFL programming. That fall, he and Berman were paired on NFL GameDay , the Sunday pregame show later rebranded as Sunday NFL Countdown , and on NFL Primetime , the Sunday night highlight program that came on after the late afternoon games and ran through 2005. A rotating cast of co-hosts cycled through the studio over the years, among them John Saunders, Trent Dilfer, and a young Robin Roberts long before Good Morning America came calling, but the show always belonged to Berman and Jackson. That ownership of Sunday nights rested on the simple fact that nothing else on television resembled what they were doing. Before streaming clips and social media, fans who spent the afternoon tethered to a single regional broadcast had no way to see the rest of the league until nightfall, and Primetime delivered the entire slate in one exhilarating hour. Berman supplied the nicknames, the sound effects and the theatrical flourishes. Jackson supplied the authority of a man who had spent 14 seasons making tackles, and his incisive, unpretentious analysis grounded the show in a way Berman’s showmanship never could have on its own. Their chemistry and evident affection for one another became the program’s hallmark, and together they set the template for what a football highlight package could be. item.title: Mark Cuban backs Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon’s sideline presence amid growing criticism
item.description: Indianapolis Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon has faced criticism for spending games on the sideline, but Mark Cuban sees no problem with her approach. The former Dallas Mavericks owner defended her after NFL fans questioned why she watches games so closely. An X account shared a video of Irsay-Gordon wearing a headset and taking notes during the recent Houston Texans game. The post questioned her presence, suggesting that having an employer watch employees throughout their workday could become frustrating. MORE: Carlie Irsay-Gordon’s major role in Colts’ Daniel Jones release revealed Super Bowl LIV champion Mitchell Schwartz pushed back against that criticism. “I do not get all the hate. She stays out of the way, she listens to the headsets, and she takes notes,” Schwartz wrote. He also compared her approach to Cuban’s time sitting behind the Mavericks’ bench. Rebilas-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Now, Cuban has responded to Schwartz by explaining why he regularly attended games from that position. “I sat behind the bench for the same reason I sat in on sales and tech meetings. So I could learn,” Cuban wrote. He explained that watching employees interact helped him understand their responses during both positive and difficult situations. It also allowed him to build stronger relationships and make himself more approachable. “I also got to hear what refs said to our coaches and players. And vice versa. Taught me a lot as well,” Cuban added. The billionaire businessman said the information helped him make better decisions. He also credited the unusual practice with giving Dallas an advantage over other teams. In an unusual incident, the match referee initially announced the toss result incorrectly. However, Pakistan A captain Abdul Samad was quick to spot the mistake and immediately pointed it out, asking the referee to recheck the decision. Following another check, the match official corrected his announcement, confirming that Pakistan A had indeed won the toss and elected to bat first. The incident, which was caught on camera, added another talking point to an already high-voltage encounter between the two neighbouring nations. India-Pakistan matches are rarely short of drama, and this time the action began even before the players took the field. item.title: New York Jets elevate veteran wide receiver ahead of Los Angeles Chargers game
item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 4: Sterling Shepard #87 of the New York Jets warms up prior to the game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on October 4, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Jets activated veteran wide receiver Sterling Shepard from the practice squad ahead of their game against the Los Angeles Chargers. Rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr. is out for today’s game with an ankle injury, leaving the Jets short at wide receiver. Sterling Shepard is a 33 year old, 5’ 10”, 195 pound wide receiver. He was originally drafted out of Oklahoma by the New York Giants with the 40th overall pick in the 2nd round of the 2016 NFL draft. Shepard was an effective receiver for the Giants early in his career. He spent the first eight years of his career with the Giants before moving on after the 2023 season. Shepard played with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2024 and 2025 before being signed as an unrestricted free agent by the Jets in 2026. Sterling Shepard has been elevated to the active roster twice this season before today. He has been targeted twice by the Jets, with one reception good for three yards. The Jets needed another body at wide receiver with Cooper out. The team has Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell active, but behind those two are Tim Patrick and Malik McClain, who are unlikely to provide much value. Unfortunately, Shepard likely has little left to offer the Jets. He will turn 34 years old in February. Shepard has not exceeded 400 receiving yards in a season, a 50% success rate, or 7 yards per target since all the way back in 2020. The Jets might be better off giving practice squad receiver Jamaal Pritchett a shot. Pritchett has excelled each of the last two training camps, only to be buried on the practice squad in the regular season. Regardless of whether the Jets elevated Shepard or Pritchett, they will be thin at wide receiver until Cooper makes it back. In the meantime, who knows, maybe Shepard has a turn back the clock performance left in his tank.

item.title: Villanova bounces back with massive 79-73 win over No. 18 Michigan
item.description: Nov 21, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Villanova Wildcats guard Tyler Perkins (4) reacts after a victory against the Michigan Wolverines at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The vibes were down after the 81-61 loss at Pittsburgh on Tuesday. Kevin Willard let the team know about his dissatisfaction in the following practices and film sessions, which yielded a 79-73 win against 18th-ranked Michigan on Saturday night. This is Willard’s first ranked win since becoming the head coach of Villanova. The Wildcats played with more energy and heart against the Wolverines than they had shown in any game prior to this, led by Elijah Crawford and Tyler Perkins. While Perkins did not shoot well (6/19 from the field, 1/6 from three), he was consistently attacking throughout the night, leading to 13 free-throw attempts (making ten). Crawford played his best 20-minute stretch in the second half against Michigan, finishing the game with 13 points, five assists and two steals (with only two turnovers). In the first half, Crawford took a few ill-advised shots, with one three-point attempt leading to an immediate seat on the bench. But in the second half, he was consistently going downhill and finishing over the enormous frontcourt of Moustapha Thiam and J.P. Estrella. Adjusting to not being asked to score as much has been a challenge for Crawford, but if he can continue to “buy in” like he said after the game, the point guard spot should be in solid hands come March. Jake Fiegen remains a flamethrower from deep, making 4/8 from three on his way to 15 points on the night. There was a two-minute stretch in the second half where Fiegen made three in a row, eventually pushing the Wildcats’ lead to 13. Followed up by a Devin Royal three and a Perkins layup, Villanova stretched its lead to a game-high 17 points with ten minutes remaining. Fiegen has been a revelation for Villanova, shooting an absurd 53.1% from the floor and 48.8% from three on the year. The aforementioned Royal played a solid game for Villanova, finishing with 11 points and seven rebounds on 4/9 from the field. More was expected of both him and Kwame Evans Jr., so this showing against the defending champs was a step in the right direction. Royal spun and laid it in with 2:26 remaining to push the Wildcats’ lead out to six. Evans Jr. played a season-high 26 minutes in this one, which I think should be the biggest takeaway. He could not finish around the rim, but he was able to make all six of his free throw attempts and grab 11 rebounds. If Villanova can get more efficiency and scoring production out of these two prized acquisitions in the offseason, there will be less pressure on the backcourt to continue to carry the weight. item.title: Kyle Whittingham calls Big House 'Rice-Eccles' in Freudian slip
item.description: Look, I hate to be that guy. But he said something dumb again. And it's all over social media. Kyle Whittingham , as he done for what feels like at least a half-dozen times, said something at a podium that only hurts the perception − and, maybe, the reality − of himself seeming aloof since being hired at Michigan football . This time, he accidentally said "Rice-Eccles" before correcting himself to say the Big House. It came minutes after Michigan's exhilarating 18-16 triple-overtime win Saturday, Nov. 21, over No. 4 UCLA (and it's third-string quarterback). The team had rushed the field. Fans stormed the field − for a second time this season (the first coming on the Hail Mary to avoid a catastrophe in Week 1 against Western Michigan). Then, Whittingham had a slip-up. And it came on his birthday, too. To his credit, Whittingham immediately caught himself and made fun of himself. But it's not the greatest look with how the season has gone for Michigan (6-5). Here's the full exchange, with video, answering a reporter's question about the defense and its seniors. It certainly doesn't like a coach who wants to get fired after a year. "First of all, a bunch of guys have played their last snaps here at Rice-Eccles − Rice-Eccles, Big House, can't believe I said that, don't think I've done that in 10 months − so, Big House. Now, don't be deceived though, we got a lot of good young players, we got some really good young guys up front in the front seven that we think are gonna be really good football players, so it's not like we're gonna be just left with nothing up front, cause we feel like we got a lot of depth there. But those guys, Enow [Etta] and Trey Pierce and of course you have the ends, John-Henry [Daley] and Dom [Nichols] have another year. And you never know. Some guys opt to test the waters of the NFL, and if it looks good to them and it sounds like they got a chance to get drafted, sometimes then plans change and they don't come back. And by the same token, some guys that walked tonight and may have a change of heart and come back, so it's not etched in stone. But bottom line is we feel like we're gonna be pretty good on defense again next year." Here’s the full video of the “Rice-Eccles - Big House” Freudian slip from Michigan Football coach Kyle Whittingham during the Postgame presser after the Wolverines 18-16 3OT win over No. 4 UCLA Saturday night: https://t.co/vvBfVGLtQJ pic.twitter.com/oHWS6mgXgB — Noah Bieniek (Bee-Nick) (@NoahB77_) November 22, 2026 This comes just over a week after Whittingham got into a back-and-forth, again perhaps intentionally, with Oregon coach Dan Lanning before playing the Ducks in Eugene (an eventual 31-7 blowout). item.title: Chelsea reportedly consider cutting losses on summer signing amid limited minutes
item.description: Chelsea reportedly consider cutting losses on summer signing amid limited minutes Chelsea are reportedly ready to let Marco Palestra leave the club in the January transfer window. Palestra signed for Chelsea from Atalanta in the summer for an initial £43m in the summer, following a standout Serie A campaign. The full-back was named Serie A Defender of the Year for 2025/26, on loan at Cagliari, but has struggled for minutes at Chelsea. The 21-year-old has started just twice in the Premier League this season and reports in Spain claim Chelsea want to replace Palestra with a more experienced option. El Nacional Catalonia are reporting that Xabi Alonso has earmarked Barcelona defender Jules Kounde as a potential signing. Barcelona are understood to be willing to consider offers for Kounde, whose role has reduced under Hansi Flick this season. The arrival of the Frenchman at Chelsea could see Palestra return to Serie A, with several Italian clubs keen. Juventus, AC Milan and Napoli are all monitoring his situation ahead of the January transfer window. item.title: Villarreal star targets Barcelona stars after defeat: ‘They affected the referee; it wasn’t a corner’
item.description: Villarreal star targets Barcelona stars after defeat: ‘They affected the referee; it wasn’t a corner’ Villarreal star Santi Comesaña refused to bite his tongue, in taking aim at his Barcelona counterparts on Sunday afternoon. This came after the Yellow Submarine were condemned to defeat at the Camp Nou. Iñigo Pérez’s troops made the trip to Catalunya’s capital a short time ago, for their post-international break return to the pitch. The visitors got off to a dream start in the clash, racing out to a two-goal advantage inside the opening seven minutes of action. The relentless pressure of Barcelona ultimately proved telling, though, as the day’s hosts roared back with three goals of their own following the interval. As alluded to above, though, one individual adamant that Villarreal were hard done by in defeat comes in the form of Santi Comesaña. Speaking to DAZN following the full-time whistle at the Camp Nou, the midfielder took full use of the opportunity to air his grievances with all of Barcelona, Real Madrid, and the team of officials on Sunday afternoon: “Barça’s first goal killed us psychologically. Gulácsi didn’t touch the ball, and they called a corner. The same thing happened to us at the Bernabéu. The pressure that Barça and Real Madrid put on referees is intense. “In the first half, there were seven Barça players protesting to the referee. item.description: Juventus v Venezia FC - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Luciano Spalletti reached a historic milestone in the Juventus dugout on Sunday, overseeing his 600th career match in Serie A. The veteran coach used the occasion to address speculation surrounding his future following a dominant second-half display against Venezia at the Allianz Stadium. Spalletti hits milestone amidst pressure Juventus manager Spalletti celebrated his 600th appearance on a Serie A bench with a comprehensive 4-0 victory over Venezia , but the afternoon began with a far more hostile atmosphere. The Bianconeri were jeered by their own supporters at half-time, with little indication that they would eventually produce such a convincing result against Davide Nicola's side. When questioned about his future and his objectives after reaching such a significant numerical landmark in Italian football, the former Napoli boss opted for a lighthearted response to the rumours. 'With everything people say, what is your career objective after hitting 600 games? Reaching the 601st is the answer, because anything can happen in football,' he joked during his post-match media duties. Woltemade provides the spark The turning point of the contest arrived at half-time when Nick Woltemade was introduced following an injury to Kerim Alajbegovic. The substitute made an immediate impact, breaking the deadlock after Weston McKennie's mishit effort fell kindly into his path. His opener sparked a remarkable turnaround, with Teun Koopmeiners adding a second before Juan Cabal headed home a third. Randal Kolo Muani then completed the 4-0 rout from the penalty spot, having won the spot-kick himself. The veteran tactician was quick to credit his players for their mental shift after the break, noting that the team finally embraced a collective philosophy that had been absent during the opening 45 minutes. 'They came on for the second half, making choices, taking decisions, with greater fluidity in the passing, trying to have a team idea,' Spalletti told DAZN Italia. Solving the Kolo Muani puzzle Despite Kolo Muani getting on the scoresheet, Spalletti admitted that the former Paris Saint-Germain attacker is still adapting to a role that does not naturally suit his instincts. 'I agree Kolo Muani feels more at ease on the left, but I need someone who can be a centre-forward with all these games,' the manager explained when discussing the tactical setup. The victory was also crucial for Juventus, taking their points tally to 21 and lifting them to sixth place in the table, five points behind fourth-placed Como. item.title: NASCAR Fans Aren’t Happy With Hendrick Motorsports After William Byron Shakeup
item.description: MARTINSVILLE, VIRGINIA - OCTOBER 31: William Byron, driver of the #24 Liberty University Chevrolet, looks on during practice for the NASCAR Cup Series Xfinity 500 at Martinsville Speedway on October 31, 2026 in Martinsville, Virginia. (Photo by Meg Oliphant/Getty Images) Getty Hendrick Motorsports has sparked strong fan reactions after confirming a major team shakeup involving William Byron and Alex Bowman ahead of the 2027 NASCAR Cup Series season. The move goes beyond a crew-chief change, with Rudy Fugle’s entire No. 24 operation set to move to Bowman’s No. 48 team. The decision leaves Byron with a new crew chief, crew members, cars and equipment after years of success with Fugle. Fans have questioned why Hendrick would break up one of its most successful recent partnerships to strengthen Bowman’s team following a difficult 2026 season. The timing has also raised questions about the future of the No. 48, as Bowman is expected to leave full-time competition after 2027. Hendrick Motorsports Makes Major Changes to Alex Bowman’s NASCAR Team Hendrick Motorsports’ offseason plans turned out to be much bigger than initially expected. Rudy Fugle is leaving William Byron’s No. 24 team for Alex Bowman’s No. 48, taking the entire crew, cars and equipment with him. Fugle and Byron spent six seasons together, building one of the strongest partnerships at Hendrick Motorsports. They recorded 16 victories, made multiple Championship 4 appearances and won the 2025 regular-season championship. The pair also won back-to-back Daytona 500 races in 2024 and 2025, making the decision to separate them a major talking point among NASCAR fans. Byron finished eighth in the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series standings and won at Martinsville. Although his season was quieter than previous campaigns, he remained a competitive driver. NASCAR Fans Question Hendrick’s Decision to Break Up Byron and Fugle The decision to move Fugle and his entire operation to Bowman has drawn criticism from fans, particularly those who believe Hendrick Motorsports is putting Byron at a disadvantage. One Byron supporter expressed frustration on Reddit, writing, “As a Byron fan, this is extremely upsetting. Don’t get me wrong, bowman is my number 2 but William is getting robbed.” Bowman struggled during the 2026 NASCAR season, finishing 26th in the standings. He failed to lead a lap and missed multiple races because of vertigo. The 2027 season will be Bowman’s final full-time year in the Cup Series, with Connor Zilisch widely expected to take over the No. 48 car in 2028. Blake Harris, Bowman’s former crew chief, is also leaving for Trackhouse Racing. Hendrick has described the changes as a strategic decision to place its personnel where they can make the biggest impact. Fugle previously worked with Bowman, while Byron will now work with Adam Wall, who is moving up from Hendrick’s O’Reilly Series program. item.description: Fox Sports broadcast analysts Tom Brady and Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes. Comparisons between Patrick Mahomes and Tom Brady often come down to championships, longevity, and what each quarterback has accomplished under pressure. Mahomes is still building his career, while Brady spent two decades setting records and winning titles. But a former Patriots teammate of Brady believes there is one physical part of the game where Mahomes has an advantage, even if matching Brady’s career remains a much bigger challenge. Willie McGinest Says Patrick Mahomes Has Edge Over Tom Brady in Arm Talent Three-time Super Bowl champion Willie McGinest discussed the comparison during an appearance on “All The Smoke Unplugged” with Matt Barnes. Barnes asked McGinest what he had noticed about Mahomes that Brady might not do as well, given his experience playing alongside the former Patriots quarterback. McGinest pointed to Mahomes’ throwing ability, particularly his arm strength and natural talent. He also suggested Brady would likely agree with that assessment. “Well, I mean, his arm, the way he throws the ball, his arm strength and his arm talent, I would say, is probably better. And Tom would probably tell you the same thing,” McGinest said. item.title: Marcell Dareus Mugshot Shows Bruises After Alabama Arrest
item.description: Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images Former NFL defensive tackle Marcell Dareus is facing allegations that he assaulted a police officer during a weekend arrest in Alabama, but his newly released mugshot is raising another question: What happened to his face? The two-time Pro Bowler appears to have sustained significant facial injuries in the booking photo obtained by the New York Post on Monday, Nov. 16. His left eye appears nearly swollen shut, while bruising, swelling, and abrasions are visible across his face. The Hoover Police Department has not publicly explained how Dareus sustained those injuries or what happened physically between the former Buffalo Bills star and the officers who arrested him. Dareus, 36, was taken into custody on Saturday, Nov. 14, following a traffic stop in Hoover, Alabama. According to police, officers initially pulled him over for allegedly driving erratically before the encounter escalated into an alleged assault and a brief pursuit. "During the stop, Mr. Dareus was non-compliant with officers, escalating his behavior to the point of assaulting an officer," a police spokesperson told The Post . Authorities claim Dareus subsequently drove away, prompting officers to follow him to his residence. Police allege that he resisted arrest a second time before being detained. Officers also reported finding marijuana in his possession. One officer reportedly received treatment at a hospital for a minor injury. Dareus was booked on charges of aggravated assault of an officer, resisting arrest, attempting to elude police, and marijuana possession. He was released on bond later that day. But while police have provided an account of Dareus' alleged conduct, the department has not publicly detailed the circumstances that left him with the injuries visible in his mugshot. Dareus has not publicly commented on the arrest. item.title: NCAA will drop pregame handshake rule at women’s tourney following Geno Auriemma-Dawn Staley incident
item.description: The NCAA women’s basketball tournament is set to scrap the rule of pregame handshakes between head coaches, per multiple reports Saturday that cited a memo sent by the Division I women’s basketball committee to all D-I programs. Per the memo, the committee reportedly “encourages” coaches to still shake hands informally ahead of team introductions at the tournament. However, it will no longer be a requirement. The change comes after the ruling blew up during the women’s Final Four a year ago when Geno Auriemma infamously had a fiery confrontation with Dawn Staley in a postgame handshake line following the Gamecocks’ semifinal victory over the Huskies. South Carolina head coach Dawn Staley, left, and UConn head coach Geno Auriemma argue after a game in Phoenix, Saturday, April 4, 2026. AP Photo/Rick Scuteri The coaches met at center court along the sidelines to shake hands when suddenly the two started jawing at one another and as things escalated, game officials and team staff got in between the two. In the immediate aftermath, Staley said “ask Geno” when asked about the incident. The 12-time national champion head coach went on to explain he took issue with Staley not showing up for their pregame handshake at center court during the coach introductions following the starting lineups. However, photographs later confirmed that they shook hands before the game. “I waited there for like three minutes,” he said after the game. “So, it is what it is.” Less than 12 hours later, Auriemma released an apology , stating there was “no excuse” for his outburst. Geno Auriemma opening up to Dawn Staley after the Final Four. AP “It’s unlike what I do and what our standard is here at Connecticut,” he said in a statement. “I want to apologize to the staff and the team at South Carolina. It was uncalled for in how I reacted.” “The story should be how well South Carolina played and I don’t want my actions to detract from that,” Auriemma added. “I’ve had a great relationship with their staff, and I sincerely want to apologize to them.” Staley and her Gamecocks went on to lose the final to UCLA, 79-51. The NCAA’s memo also detailed that game clocks are required to display tenths of a second on shot clocks for the 2027 opening round, first and second rounds of the tournament. Dawn Staley threatened to “beat Geno’s ass” after the interaction. Joe Camporeale-Imagn Images That has already been a requirement at regional games and for the Final Four. By 2028, it will be a requirement for each round. Additionally, there will no longer be locker room media access nor mandatory press conferences between the Sweet 16 and Elite Eight at the regional locations. Pregame interviews with coaches at those events have also been discarded. The NCAA men’s and women’s tournaments are expanding to 76 teams in 2027. The top 16 seeds will be revealed on March 13, the day before Selection Sunday.

item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team.
